answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through costly, auditable work: for example, a buyer escrows payment, a task produces a verifiable result, and a randomly selected reviewer stakes funds that are slashed if an audit finds fraud. New identities start with no history, so splitting into a shale-colored swarm or naming each bot raven earns nothing; Sybils must repeatedly buy real tasks and risk bonded capital. The signal of trust is accumulated success under independent review, not account count, making attacks expensive rather than impossible.
